synopsis.short: Ben Harper is a Chicago chef living deliberately small — present, in love, nothing like his father. When a foundation gala honors his father's Paris legend, Ben skips it and flies to Paris instead. He finds the man still cooking in a back room, still chasing the next star as if the last one meant nothing. And he finds the same hunger alive in himself.
synopsis.long:
Ben Harper keeps a secret: he is Benjamin Harper Jr., named for a father who earned a Michelin star in Paris and vanished the same night. Ben has spent his adult life in Chicago doing the opposite — cooking without ambition, staying put, growing a relationship slowly and without fanfare.

When a culinary foundation announces a gala to honor his father's ghost, Ben doesn't go. He flies to Paris. He traces his father through former kitchens, old colleagues, the woman left behind. What he expected was a reckoning. What he finds is a mirror: a man still cooking in a small room, still reaching for the next recognition, the last one already meaningless. The obsession didn't make the star. The star fed the obsession.

Ben sees himself in that room. The precision he can't turn off. The restlessness. The instinct to leave before anything gets warm.

The novel's final tension is not forgiveness but choice. Ben comes home to the romance he's let grow — the life that asked only that he stay — and stays.
